title: Lockheeds Pension Fund Sold Apple Stock and Bought Alibaba - Barron's

organizations.name: laura kammermann lockheed martin investment management co.

text:
Lockheed’s Pension Fund Dumped Apple for Alibaba By Feb. 6, 2019 7:00 a.m. ET Order Reprints Photograph by Jack Taylor/Getty Images Text size
The pension fund at defense contractor Lockheed Martin (ticker: LMT) unloaded almost all of its Apple (AAPL) stock in the fourth quarter, plowing cash into another tech darling, Alibaba Group Holding (BABA), according to disclosures made last week. Bill Gross, who made Pimco a powerhouse but saw uneven returns the last four years, announced his retirement Monday. Justin Baer looks back on one of the most celebrated careers in the history of money management. Photo Illustration: Laura Kammermann
Lockheed Martin Investment Management Co. said that in addition to slashing its Apple holdings, the pension reduced the stake in Exxon Mobil (XOM) by more than half. It also bought American depositary receipts of Alibaba and stock in Boston Scientific (BSX), two securities it hadn’t owned in the third quarter. LMIMCo disclosed the stock trades in a form filed to the Securities and Exchange Commission.
Lockheed declined to comment.
LMIMCo sold 150,000 Apple shares in the fourth quarter, cutting its investment to only 13,670 shares of the iPhone maker. Barron’s suggested last month that Apple should buy videogame firm Nintendo , which we noted is “its stylistic twin in Asia.” Apple stock was up 10.4% so far this year through Tuesday’s close, just ahead of the S&P 500 ’s 10.2% rise.
Exxon stock is also just ahead of the index so far in 2019 with a gain of 10.9%. Barron’s has noted recent changes at the company, including the participation of its CEO for the first time on an earnings call . Lockheed’s pension sold 12,850 shares of the energy giant in the fourth quarter to end the year with only 9,650 shares.
LMIMCo bought 21,000 Alibaba ADRs in the fourth quarter. The Chinese Internet giant lost a fifth of its market value in U.S. trading last year, but the ADRs had gained 25% in 2019 as of Tuesday’s close.
The fund bought 61,800 Boston Scientific shares in the fourth quarter, another new investment. Shares of the medical-devices company have risen only 7.5% year to date, but that follows a 43% surge in 2018.
